title: Ролик из Риги  (The Video from Riga)

segments.t: In the kitchen of Claude Monet, Senya and Fedya browse online videos between orders and stumble upon a shocking clip. The video shows their new head chef German in a violent brawl, and Viktor Petrovich immediately recognizes another man in the footage. Let's listen to their discovery in Russian.
Это что, наш Герман, что ли?
Now let's examine how the cooks uncover the video of German line by line.
'They ordered a horsemeat steak out there.' An indefinite third-person plural past verb reports a customer order without naming a specific subject.
'Look, there is one more video clip.' Senya uses a singular imperative of looking to point out another video clip on the screen.
'It has the exact same title.' A possessive genitive phrase introduces a neuter singular noun meaning title or name.
Это что, наш Герман, что ли?
'Wait, is that our German or what?' Colloquial question particles frame Senya's disbelief as he recognizes the new head chef on screen.
'I wonder where all this took place?' An impersonal introductory adverb meaning interesting leads into an indirect question about location.
'Stop it, I know him well.' Chef Barinov commands Senya to pause the video using a singular perfective imperative.
'He used to work in Riga.' The city name Riga takes the prepositional case ending after the preposition meaning in.
'That is my acquaintance Markus.' A substantivized masculine adjective functions as a noun meaning acquaintance or friend.
'Give me the phone, I will call him.' A singular imperative of giving precedes a perfective future verb governing a dative pronoun.
'Hello, Markus, hi there, my friend.' Barinov greets his Latvian colleague warmly on the phone using standard telephone greetings.
'Tell me about this German.' A perfective imperative of telling takes a dative recipient and a colloquial accusative preposition meaning about.
'Thank you very much for the information.' The preposition for governs the feminine accusative singular noun meaning information. Let's hear the whole kitchen conversation again from start to finish.
Это что, наш Герман, что ли?

Viktor Petrovich identifies his Riga acquaintance Markus in the video and calls him right away to get the full story. Notice the imperative verb meaning stop and the past-tense verb meaning worked. See you in the next scene.
